_comment: Provenance record for the photography in robas-law-website/assets/photos/. Not rendered on the site — kept so the source of every image is documented if it is ever questioned. The Unsplash License permits free commercial use without attribution (https://unsplash.com/license). All six were downloaded, desaturated to 55% and contrast-adjusted to match the site palette, then served from this repo rather than hotlinked.
_clientLogoNote: Client logos sourced September 2026. Unlike the photography above, these are third-party TRADEMARKS, displayed as a client reference. The firm's own client relationship is the basis for showing them — confirm with the client before adding any new one. Each entry records where the file came from so the use can be evidenced if questioned. The seven older logos (hapoalim, beinleumi, pagi, manpower, hinuma-motors, obzotek, shivuk-hamea) predate this record and came from material the firm already held.

clientLogos.note: Inline <svg> in the site header, extracted verbatim. Artwork reads AGIMER LEASING / אגימר ליסינג ומימון בע״מ.
Deliberately the -B (black) variant. The site's own header serves logo-W, a white knockout that would be invisible on the white cell.
Artwork itself reads מ.ל.ב — המרכז לפיקוח ובקרת זכויות עובדים בע״מ, which is the full registered name.
Registered as וי.בי.אס אחזקות בע״מ. logo-1 is the navy/orange variant; the default logo.png is a white knockout.
Identity rests on the domain and page title, not on the artwork: the mark reads only 'md LTD' with no company name.

GASPRO is the group's trading mark. The registry holds no company literally named גזפרו בע״מ — it holds גזפרו בילו בע״מ (514042084) and גזפרו ליסינג ישראל בע״מ (514971324) at one Emek Hefer address, and gaspro.co.il's footer claims copyright for גזפרו בע״מ. Ask Lior which entity is the client. Only 280x102 is published, the smallest file in the set.

firmOwned.note: Reception desk and waiting area. This is the photograph the whole palette was sampled from: ink desk, oak floor, ochre chairs, the sea triptych. Not desaturated — the licensed imagery is graded toward this, not the other way round.
Entrance with the LR monogram wall.

licensed.why: Warm desk and blinds; matches the oak in the office palette. Used instead of a portrait, since there are none.
Abstract light through sheer fabric; a quiet break with no subject matter to misread.
Echoes the sea triptych hanging in the firm's own reception.
Institutional architecture, chosen over the usual gavel or scales imagery.
Israeli apartment building, the actual subject of most of the firm's property work.
Nib and paper detail: signature and authentication without stock-photo people.
